# Methamphetamine from Cold-Medicine Ingredients

The classic route uses **pseudoephedrine** (the active decongestant in products like Sudafed) or, in older formulations, **phenylephrine** (the original Sudofed ingredient). Both are structurally very close to methamphetamine, differing only by a single hydroxyl (–OH) group on the carbon chain.

## The Core Chemistry

The transformation is a **reduction**: the –OH group on the C2 position is replaced by a hydrogen atom.

```
Pseudoephedrine          →        Methamphetamine
(1R,2S)-2-methyl-4-(2-phenyl-1-phenylbutan-2-ol)
        |
   C2–OH  →  C2–H
```

# From Cold Medicine to Meth: The Pseudoephedrine Route

The most direct "cold medicine" connection to methamphetamine is the decongestant **pseudoephedrine** (the active ingredient in products like Sudafed). Pseudoephedrine is only one chemical step away from methamphetamine.

## Why This Works

| Compound | Structure (simplified) |
|---|---|
| Pseudoephedrine | C₆H₅–CH(**OH**)–CH(NHCH₃)–CH₃ |
| Methamphetamine | C₆H₅–CH₂–CH(NHCH₃)–CH₃ |

The only difference is the **–OH** group on the benzylic carbon, which must be replaced by a **–H**. Everything else (the aromatic ring, the methylamino group, the methyl group) is already in place.
